newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Thousands will need food aid in Mozambique - U.N..
newsitem.headline: Thousands will need food aid in Mozambique - U.N..

text.p: Tens of thousands of flood victims and rural poor in Mozambique are in urgent need of food aid until the next harvest in September after heavy floods destroyed their crops, the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) said on Friday.

It said cereal production for the country was however expected to rise by 11 percent in 1997 following increased planted area. But this was not enough to feed the estimated 170,000 people who lost their crops in the floods earlier this year.

"Despite the good harvest, a total of 172,000 people will need 10,114 tonnes of food assistance until the second smaller harvest in September," the WFP said in a statement after a food supply assessment mission to Mozambique with the Food and Agriculture Organisation.
"Some 72,000 people may require assistance for three months if the harvest is not successful," it added.
The U.N. body said about 103,000 hectares of crops were destroyed in the floods in the central provinces of Sofala, Tete and Zambezia.
